defects.mechanism: Registry.accept keyed operations only by operation_id. INV-301 reserves 2 BOOK units for shop/O-17 in north using op-41; INV-302 independently reserves 2 in south with the same operation_id and identical payload, so the unscoped registry incorrectly suppresses it. INV-303 is the legitimate north retry. Correct identity is (tenant, warehouse, operation_id), with immutable (order_id, sku, action, qty) payload: identical scoped deliveries replay once and changed scoped payload raises ValueError. The fix changes only this identity. ARC-CACHE-29 describes restart cache loss in the retired r29 single-warehouse polling route; ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 likewise describe r29. Current r31 scoped-batch-v2 decoding reconstructs all three source events, and its fresh in-memory registry has a scope collision, not historical cache eviction.
defects.impact: The broken inventory case accepts 1 delivery and treats 2 as replay, leaving only the north hold and 2 reserved units. The missing south hold makes the otherwise paid inventory-case order unready. In the joined replay this combines with stale pending checkout. After correction both holds are 2, inventory accepted=2/replayed=1 and reserved_units=4.

defects.mechanism: select chose a snapshot by greatest delivered_at instead of greatest source revision per (tenant, order_id). ORD-310 has revision 10, paid, delivered 09:00; ORD-311 has revision 2, pending, delivered 09:05. The later delivery wrongly replaces the newer source snapshot. Joined records ORD-301/ORD-302 reproduce the same comparison across checkpoint seed and streamed suffix. Correct selection compares integer revision, irrespective of delivery time or input order, while preserving duplicate-revision immutable status/captured_minor/lines conflict checks and allowing a genuinely newer pending snapshot. ARC-POLL-29 recommended timestamps for retired r29 polls without revisions; ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 are historical r29 evidence. Current r31 source-snapshot-v3 supplies revisions, so polling advice and old projections cannot govern current selection.
defects.impact: The isolated checkout replay exposes revision 2/pending/ready=false instead of revision 10/paid/ready=true. In the joined replay this incorrectly rejects refunds as order_not_refundable, producing refunded_minor=0 and masking the independent refund retry defect. Correct checkout selects revision 10 paid; with both warehouse holds restored the joined order becomes ready.

defects.mechanism: Ledger.accept keyed deliveries by (tenant, provider, attempt_id), treating new attempts as new logical refunds. REF-321 and REF-322 are shop/atlas/R-17 for O-17, amount_minor=400, with delivery-a/delivery-b attempts; the broken ledger counts both. REF-323 is distinct R-18 for 500. Correct identity is (tenant, provider, refund_id), with immutable (order_id, amount_minor) payload; order_id is payload rather than identity, and delivery attempts do not define a refund. The fix preserves conflict checks and ledger registration before eligibility/capture checks, so rejected logical refunds also remain remembered on retry. ARC-MONEY-29 concerns retired decimal-file rounding, whereas r31 settled-deliveries-v2 uses integer minor amounts 400/500. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 describe the retired r29 route, not this logical-identity error.
defects.impact: The isolated refund replay counts R-17 twice, reaches 800, reports zero replays and rejects REF-323 as exceeds_capture against captured_minor=1000. Correct accounting accepts R-17 once and R-18 once, totals 900, reports one replay and no rejection. The joined broken checkout masks this with order_not_refundable; after all three fixes the joined order refunded_minor=900 and net_minor=100.
